overall: Atlanta is experiencing a hot, humid Fourth of July with the running max stuck at 91.4°F since approximately 13:00 ET — over three hours of flat temperature trend despite peak afternoon insolation and a Heat Advisory in effect until 8 PM EDT. The sky is partially obscured (62% cloud fraction, SCT ceiling) and dewpoints remain elevated near 71-73°F, suggesting boundary layer moisture and cloud shading are capping daytime heating well below model guidance. A faint 30-minute velocity uptick (+3.6°F/hr) offers a marginal warming signal, but the 2-hour velocity is flat at 0.0°F/hr.
forecast_obs_notes: There is a stark disagreement between the obs-driven INTRADAY model and NWP guidance: GFS/ECMWF/HRRR/NBM are all forecasting a daily high of 93.6–95.8°F while observations have stalled 2–4°F below that range for several hours. The NWP models predict peak timing around 15.0–17.0h ET (we are now at 15:50), leaving a narrow window for a late-afternoon surge, but the sustained flat trend through the historical peak hours makes the full model forecast increasingly unlikely to verify.
max_temp_prediction: With the running max flat at 91.4°F for 3+ hours, peak timing nearly expired (mean model peak at 15.8h, current time 15:50), and cloud cover restraining heating, the TMAX is most likely to land in the 92–94°F range rather than the 95–96°F the NWS text and NWP models project. A late-afternoon thermal pulse (HRRR peaks at 17:00h) remains possible but would need to overcome both the momentum of a stalled temperature curve and increasing cloud/storm activity. On the active EVEN bucket market, the 92-93F and 90-91F buckets carry the highest observational support, though given the aggressive model consensus the 94-95F bucket cannot be ruled out; confidence is moderate-low given the large model-vs-obs spread. Best single-point estimate is 93.0°F.
